newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FIGURE SKATING-FASSI'S WIDOW WATCHES SKATER.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-FASSI'S WIDOW WATCHES SKATER.

text.p: Christa Fassi, faithful to one of her husband's last requests, accompanied American Nicole Bobek at the women's short programme in the world figure skating championships on Friday.
Carlo Fassi, Christa's husband and Bobek's coach, died of a heart attack on Thursday, eve of the women's event.
"One of his last words was asking Christa to be with me during the competition," Bobek said.
Yet it was asking too much of Bobek to give a vintage performance after going through an emotional wringer during the preceding 24 hours.
Bobek had switched coaches 10 times during her career but seemed to have found contentment with Fassi, whom she joined for the second time last summer.
Sadly, she gave an erratic display and finished eighth. She did a poor combination jump and almost fell on a triple toe loop.
She received scores around 4.9 and 5.0 for technique but did better for artistry with marks up to 5.7 out of the maximum of 6.0.
"It meant so much to have Christa with me. I know how hard it was on her," the American said.
"My warm-up felt great and I was very strong. But right before I did my programme I looked at Christa and began crying.
"My mind was racing but I was able to refocus my energy into what I needed to do. But my short was not great. My landings were not strong," she said.

"It was better than at the nationals, so I will build on that going into the free skating." She was sixth in the short at the U.S. national championships before climbing to third to earn her place here.
Bobek said she was helped by the crowd on Friday.
"I felt their warmth and support," she said. "Looking up to the flags waving and the cheers was great support. I could feel their understanding of what I am going through."
